case_name: Deepak S/O Ranveer Singh vs State Of Rajasthan (2023:Rj-Jp:23924)

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Deepak S/o Ranveer Singh, Aged About 21 Years, R/o Mahrawar, Police Kumher, District Bharatpur (Raj.)

facts_of_case: Petitioner has filed this miscellaneous bail application under Section 438 Cr.P.C who is having apprehension of his arrest in connection with FIR No.86/2023 PS Kumher, District Bharatpur for offences under Sections 363, 366 & 376 IPC.

legal_principles.principle: Anticipatory bail application can be entertained after filing of the charge-sheet.
legal_principles.held: In case of Bharat Choudhary (supra), it was held by Hon'ble Apex Court that application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. for grant of anticipatory bail will be maintainable after charge-sheet is filed or cognizance is taken.
cited_cases: Bharat Choudhary & Anr. Vs. State of Bihar & Anr., (2003) 8 SCC 77

legal_principles.principle: The issuance of warrant under Section 37 of the Police Act does not mean that the accused is absconding.
legal_principles.held: Merely issuance of warrant under Section 37 of the Police Act does not mean that the petitioner is absconding.

legal_principles.principle: The person who is 'absconding' and declared as 'proclaimed offender' is not entitled to seek anticipatory bail application normally.
legal_principles.held: It was made clear in the aforesaid case of Lavesh (supra) that when the accused is absconding and has also been declared 'proclaimed offender', case of granting anticipatory bail does not arise.
cited_cases: Lavesh Vs. State (NCT of Delhi), (2012) 8 SCC 730

legal_principles.principle: Anticipatory bail can be entertained even if the charge-sheet has been filed.
legal_principles.held: In case of Ravindra Saxena (supra), Hon'ble Apex Court considering the same situation held that after filing of the charge-sheet, anticipatory bail application can be entertained.
cited_cases: Ravindra Saxena Vs. State of Rajasthan, (2010) 1 SCC 684

outcome.final_order: Custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not warranted in this case.

keywords: Latin maxim: actus me invito non facit actum
